I've been working this land in Quzhou for two decades. I know the North China Plain — hot summers, cold winters, and never enough rain when you need it. My well saves me when the sky doesn't cooperate.

Eight mu isn't much, but with 10 people in the household and some of the younger ones in the city now, I manage with machines more than I used to. The wheat-maize rotation is the only system that makes sense here. Same land, two crops a year — that's how you make 8 mu feed a family and still have something to sell.

For **wheat**, I plant in October on all 8 mu. I've switched to improved varieties — the extension station pushed Jimai lines hard and I've seen the yields myself. I'll do rotary tillage after the maize harvest to chop up the stalks and prepare a proper seedbed. I apply base fertilizer before sowing and topdress nitrogen at the jointing stage. Four irrigations: pre-winter to help establishment, jointing, heading, and grain filling. Stripe rust and powdery mildew hit us some years, so three pesticide passes — herbicide early spring, fungicide at heading, aphid control if needed.

For **maize**, I go in right after the wheat combine in June. No-till direct seeding — it saves time and keeps the soil from drying out in that brutal June heat. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar, same as my neighbors. Maize is heavier on nitrogen so I push that up a bit, split between base and side-dress at V6. Summer gets more rainfall so three irrigations is usually enough — seedling establishment, tasseling, and grain fill if it's dry. Two pesticide applications: herbicide and one pass for corn borer or aphids.

At 65, I don't experiment much. I've learned what this soil gives back when you treat it right.
